newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's per capita power production at 1,388 kwh.
newsitem.headline: Iran's per capita power production at 1,388 kwh.

text.p: Iran's per capita electricity production stands at 1,388 kilowatt hours and it plans to boost generation by starting work on four major power projects this year, the Iranian news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.
It quoted Energy Minister Bijan Namdar Zanganeh as saying Iran set aside 20,000 billion rials ($11.4 billion) for power projects in its 1995-2000 development plan.
Hydroelectric plants with total capacity of 5,400 megawatts were being built and work was starting in the year from March 20 on four projects with total capacity of 3,000 megawatts, he said.
IRNA quoted Zanganeh as saying Iran's power production, equal to yearly power generation of about 83.3 billion kilowatt hours, had risen by about 51 percent in the past seven years.
Consumption stood at 82 billion kilowatt-hours in the Iranian year that ended on March 19, the agency added.
About 94 percent of Iran's population of about 60 million were provided with electricity, 40 percent of which was being used by the manufacturing sector, Zanganeh said.

"Turning to cooperation with foreign companies, he said the country will cooperate with highly efficient companies that are ready to transfer technical know-how to Iran and enter into long-term cooperation with the Energy Ministry," IRNA reported.
Russia has signed a $800 million deal with Iran to complete a nuclear power plant in the Gulf port of Bushehr which Iranian officials have said is expected to go on line in the year 2000.

An Energy Ministry official has said that Iran sells 200 million kilowatts of power to the Azeri enclave of Nakhichevan for $10 million a year and has signed a $50 million deal to provide one billion kilowatts annually to Armenia.
($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state budget accounts)
